checklist.item: Sill plate is preservative-treated or naturally durable, on a sill gasket or capillary break, and anchored to the foundation with size and spacing noted.
checklist.why: Untreated wood on concrete rots; anchor bolts are structural.

checklist.item: Wood framing and sheathing are at least 8 in (200 mm) above exposed earth, and siding at least 6 in (150 mm).
checklist.why: Wood near soil decays and invites termites.

checklist.item: The water barrier laps over flashing or a weep screed at the base so water leaves the wall above the foundation.
checklist.why: Water trapped at the plate rots it from behind the cladding.

checklist.item: Shear wall nailing, hold-downs and straps are referenced to the structural drawings.
checklist.why: Architectural and structural bases must agree.

checklist.item: Insulation, air sealing at the plate and slab-edge or stem-wall insulation are shown.
checklist.why: The plate line is a major air leak.

checklist.item: Termite protection or inspection gap is noted where local practice requires it.
